title: Fix the open ranges
starter:
type node =
  | Range of string
  | Lit of int
  | Add of node * node
  | End of node * string

let rec opens (n : node) : string list =
  match n with
  | Range _ -> []
  | Lit _ -> []
  | Add (a, b) -> List.sort_uniq compare (opens a @ opens b)
  | End (e, _) -> opens e
hints: A range is open in itself, so `Range name` should give a list holding that one name.
`End (e, name)` closes one range: take `opens e` and drop `name` from it.
`List.filter (fun x -> x <> name) (opens e)` keeps every name except the closed one.

answer.code:
type node =
  | Range of string
  | Lit of int
  | Add of node * node
  | End of node * string

let rec opens (n : node) : string list =
  match n with
  | Range name -> [name]
  | Lit _ -> []
  | Add (a, b) -> List.sort_uniq compare (opens a @ opens b)
  | End (e, name) -> List.filter (fun x -> x <> name) (opens e)
answer.explain: A `Range` is open in itself, so it returns its own name. `Add` takes the union of its two sides. `End` returns what is open in its effect with the closed range filtered out. `Lit` depends on no range.
